songs.title: 내릴 역
songs.description: Early-2000s Korean bright midtempo pop, sung in Korean by a bright male mid-range voice, B3 to E4, no female vocals, never belted, never strained, no rasp. B flat major, 108 BPM, light and rolling. A warm electric piano comps short chords and leads, an acoustic guitar strumming eighths, a clean electric arpeggio answering between lines. Light kit: closed hi-hat in eighths, shaker, handclaps on two and four. Small close-miked strings, airy and sweet. The bass steps up under each chorus line into a bright major seventh, the one bright event. Warm smiling delivery, slightly behind the beat, small vibrato at line ends only, no crescendo. The voice carries every line to the end, no long instrumental tail. The backing track has a dark top end with no cymbal sizzle. The voice keeps its natural breath and air, close-miked and present. Lead vocal clearly in front of the band. No English lyrics, no autotune, no trot, no K-pop gloss. Bright airy modern mix, not retro.

songs.title: Until Only the Room Is Left
songs.description: Free rhythm timed by breathing: a short phrase, then a stop, then the room goes quiet. One solo daegeum, a large Korean bamboo transverse flute, in its low register. Each phrase is shorter than the one before: three notes, then two, then one, then only breath. Only five pitches in the whole piece: A, C, D, E, G. No other notes, no augmented second, no bent quarter tones. Air enters each note slowly, no tonguing, membrane buzz absent. Close and dry, one mic in a small wooden room, short tail, nothing held underneath, only room tone in the gaps. Every phrase settles on the low A; at the end of a long tone the pitch falls slowly to the next note of the scale. The figure returns, never the same length twice. Sleep music. No vocals. One instrument alone: no ensemble, no second instrument, no percussion, no piano, no guitar, no strings, no synth, no pad, no drone. No rain, no nature sounds. No crescendo, no climax.

songs.title: 젓가락
songs.description: Early-2000s Korean sunny acoustic pop, sung in Korean by a male mid-range voice, A3 to D4, warm and easygoing, no female vocals, never belted, never strained, no rasp. D major, 92 BPM, light and walking. A steel-string acoustic guitar strums the pulse and leads, a bright piano answering between lines with single notes. Light kit: brushed backbeat, tambourine, shaker. Small close-miked strings from the first bar, airy and sweet. A bright secondary dominant lifts every chorus, the one bright event. Warm smiling delivery, slightly behind the beat, small vibrato at line ends only, one decibel at most in the last chorus, no crescendo. The backing track has a dark top end with no cymbal sizzle. The voice keeps its natural breath and air, close-miked and present. Lead vocal clearly in front of the band. No English lyrics, no autotune, no trot, no K-pop gloss, no dance-pop synths. Bright airy modern mix, not retro.
